title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Close gaps between Redwood's tool-calling surface and OpenAI's function/tool calling compatibility layer. Several customers expect exact semantics for tool_choice, mapped tool schemas, and consistent tool message formatting when falling back to internal tool invocations. This PR implements the runtime and API compatibility changes to align behavior and surface precise diagnostics for compatibility testing.

What this changes: implements tool schema mapping (allowing Redwood tool descriptors to be coerced/mapped to OpenAI-style JSON Schema descriptions), formalizes tool_choice semantics returned via the OpenAI-compatible API (including deterministic selection when multiple tools match), and standardizes how tool messages are formatted and streamed back to clients (preserves source tool metadata and structured args).

Implementation details: The changes span three areas: 1) openai_compat layer: new mapper module that translates Redwood tool descriptors (type hints, arg schemas, enums) into OpenAI-style function schemas; 2) runtime selection: deterministic tool_choice ordering when multiple tools are eligible, and a tie-break policy configurable by customer via route config; 3) message formatting: tool-invocation responses are emitted as two-phase messages (tool_call with name+arguments then tool_result with structured output), matching OpenAI expected event shapes and streaming tokens for arguments when large.

Backward compatibility: The default behavior is non-breaking for existing Redwood API consumers unless they opt into the openai_compat API surface. When openai_compat mode is enabled for a route, consumers will see tool_choice and function schemas in the same shape as OpenAI responses. Migration notes included in docs.

Testing: unit tests for mapper, deterministic selection policy, and formatter; integration tests exercising streaming semantics with large argument payloads; cross-compat tests against existing OpenAI compatibility harness. CI shows full test suite passing after a transient lint failure fixed in a follow-up commit.

Rollout: feature gated behind route-level `openai_compat: true`. Start with canary rollout to internal dedicated clusters, then opt-in customers, then global enablement.

Checklist:
- [x] mapper implementation and unit tests
- [x] deterministic tool_choice policy and tests
- [x] streaming message format + integration tests
- [x] docs and examples updated
- [x] migration notes

Related: Linear ENG-8721 (tooling compat), ENG-8789 (streaming stability), PM-341 (product requirements).
